questions.q: What does it mean for two components to be 'tightly coupled'?
options: They communicate only through platform events
A change to one forces a change to the other, or one can't function without the other being available at the same moment
They are both deployed in the same Salesforce org
They share the same Apex class
questions.explain: Tight coupling means components depend directly on each other's internals or availability, so a change or outage in one directly affects the other.

questions.q: What is 'fan-out' in an event-driven design?
options: A single subscriber listening to many different event channels at once
One published event reaching multiple independent subscribers, each reacting on its own without knowing about the others
A platform event that gets converted into multiple custom object records
The process of unsubscribing from a channel
questions.explain: Fan-out is one event being received by several independent subscribers simultaneously, each running its own logic unaware of the others.

questions.q: In orchestration, how is a multi-step process coordinated?
options: There is no coordinator; each step reacts to events on its own
A central coordinator (such as a Flow) explicitly calls each step in order and waits for each to finish
Steps run in a random order determined by the event bus
Each step publishes its own event with no caller involved at all
questions.explain: Orchestration relies on one central coordinator that knows and explicitly drives the entire sequence of steps, waiting for each to complete before calling the next.

questions.q: In a choreographed process, how does Component C know when to start its work?
options: A central orchestrator calls Component C directly
Component C polls Component B's database every few seconds
Component C subscribes to the event Component B publishes when its own work finishes, and reacts to that
Component C runs on a fixed daily schedule regardless of upstream events
questions.explain: In choreography, each component only knows what event to listen for; Component C reacts to the event published by Component B, with no central coordinator involved.

questions.q: What is a real cost of choosing a choreographed, event-driven design over an orchestrated one?
options: Choreography always runs slower than orchestration
Choreography makes it harder to see and reason about the whole process in one place, since no single component holds the full sequence
Choreography cannot use platform events at all
Choreography requires every subscriber to be written in the same programming language
questions.explain: Choreography trades away the single-place visibility orchestration gives you — understanding the full process means tracing through multiple independent subscribers rather than reading one coordinator.
